interpretation: Scores are editorial judgments over source-bound capability evidence and current audience-demand signals. They are not measured audience performance. Rank determines the recommended direction order, not production admission.

ranking.storyTitle: The agent was ready to act. The boundary decided whether it could.
ranking.hook: Before this AI agent touches a tool, it has to survive its own control plane.
ranking.humanStory: An operator delegates real work, watches a live interlock reject an unmanaged probe, allow a declared action, and hold anything outside the proven boundary.
ranking.whyNext: Agent autonomy, reliability, and oversight are current enterprise concerns. The seven-scenario circuit gives us identity, denial, permission, adjudication, operator control, and fail-closed behavior in one visible story.
ranking.directionRisk: A cyber-lock visual would flatten the capability. The film must show an operator retaining authority while useful work still proceeds.
ranking.recommendedPackage: 90-second flagship film, 30-second Short, interactive tool-call decision demo, evidence story
ranking.capabilityTitle: Govern one agent session through an admitted hook interlock

ranking.storyTitle: The architecture was correct. Now people could finally see it.
ranking.hook: What if every invisible software capability could explain itself as a film?
ranking.humanStory: An enterprise stakeholder receives a faithful human-readable experience from an admitted capsule, challenges it, and reaches an explicit review disposition.
ranking.whyNext: This is the mission explaining and testing itself. Its fourteen scenarios cover scene authority, deterministic visuals, creative assets, narration, assembly, fidelity evaluation, review, revision, and evidence.
ranking.directionRisk: A self-referential product demo could feel abstract. Anchor the story in a stakeholder who cannot approve what they cannot understand.
ranking.recommendedPackage: Product manifesto film, before/after explainer, interactive capability-to-media compiler, training lesson

ranking.storyTitle: Five models worked the problem. None of them ran the show.
ranking.hook: This is what a multi-model AI team looks like when every role has limits.
ranking.humanStory: A team depends on a complex answer while author, reviewer, and specialist stages cross providers, preserve isolated context, validate outputs, stop on limits, and resume from evidence.
ranking.whyNext: Multi-agent and multi-provider systems have strong current topic demand. Fourteen scenarios create a dense but legible competence spectacle with roles, dependencies, budgets, switches, cancellation, and resumption.
ranking.directionRisk: Do not personify models as a generic boardroom. Show the human work product getting stronger as bounded roles contribute and challenge it.
ranking.recommendedPackage: Two-minute systems film, role-conveyor simulator, architecture infographic, practitioner training module
ranking.capabilityTitle: Execute governed multi-model multi-provider role conveyors

ranking.storyTitle: The model hit its limit. The role kept moving.
ranking.hook: A provider ran out of capacity halfway through the job. Watch what stayed unchanged.
ranking.humanStory: A critical role encounters quota or availability failure; eligible alternatives are checked in order while meaning, context, budget, and user-facing identity remain stable.
ranking.whyNext: This extends the proven narration story into a general reliability law. Existing visual language, provider entities, and audience framing can be reused without repeating the same product outcome.
ranking.directionRisk: It is adjacent to the completed narration film. The new story must center role continuity across a larger task rather than another audio recovery.
ranking.recommendedPackage: 60-second capability film, failure-matrix demo, provider-switch infographic, reliability article

ranking.storyTitle: The rebuild failed. Nothing approved was lost.
ranking.hook: She stopped the regeneration halfway through. Every known-good byte came back.
ranking.humanStory: A language maintainer attempts a high-stakes regeneration, abandons it when closure fails, and verifies that admitted and untargeted work is byte-identical after rollback.
ranking.whyNext: This has the clearest standalone human fear-to-relief arc in the remaining estate. One scenario, two mechanics, and explicit before/after digests make it unusually cheap to direct and prove.
ranking.directionRisk: Byte identity is visually invisible. The human work, interrupted regeneration, rollback, and restored project must carry the experience while digests provide proof.
ranking.recommendedPackage: 45-second film, visual before/after proof, rollback demo, maintainer training card
ranking.capabilityTitle: Preserve admitted projection on incomplete regeneration

ranking.storyTitle: An entire capability collapsed into one portable, provable object.
ranking.hook: This file can reveal a whole capability—and prove it is still the same one.
ranking.humanStory: A maintainer needs to move, inspect, and reproduce an admitted capability without losing contracts, identity, or lineage; the capsule collapses and reveals the minimum sufficient representation.
ranking.whyNext: Capsules are SideFX's most ownable visual and commercial concept. Eight scenarios support transformation, portability, self-description, minimality, content addressing, and deterministic reveal.
ranking.directionRisk: Avoid a magic-box metaphor. The visual must expose what is retained, what is excluded, and why the digest matters.
ranking.recommendedPackage: Brand-defining film, interactive capsule reveal, anatomy infographic, technical article
ranking.capabilityTitle: Manage one capability capsule through collapse and reveal

ranking.storyTitle: The agents disagreed. The system refused to guess.
ranking.hook: More AI opinions do not create truth. A governed convergence round might.
ranking.humanStory: An author faces competing candidate changes; deterministic rules normalize every finding into an advanced, repairable, or blocked disposition and expose only the bounded repair surface.
ranking.whyNext: The story meets current interest in agentic coding while differentiating SideFX from ungoverned agent swarms. Nine scenarios provide visible conflict, evaluation, repair, and convergence.
ranking.directionRisk: Do not imply consensus equals correctness. Deterministic conformance evidence, not agent agreement, must resolve the round.
ranking.recommendedPackage: 75-second film, convergence workbench, findings infographic, author training lesson
ranking.capabilityTitle: Govern one authoring convergence round deterministically

ranking.storyTitle: The build was green. It still was not published.
ranking.hook: A local success means nothing until the exact change survives mainline.
ranking.humanStory: An authorized publisher carries a sealed change through baseline comparison, renewed proof, atomic admission, mainline lineage, and observation while preserving the prior estate on failure.
ranking.whyNext: This gives the platform a sharp before/after definition of done. Five scenarios create a strong journey from candidate confidence to durable public reality.
ranking.directionRisk: Git ceremony alone is visually weak. Center the people waiting on the capability and the difference between local belief and shared reality.
ranking.recommendedPackage: 60-second release film, mainline journey infographic, publication evidence story, operator checklist
ranking.capabilityTitle: Publish one sealed capability change to mainline

ranking.storyTitle: The AI made a claim. The ledger made it answerable.
ranking.hook: Can your AI prove what happened without turning missing evidence into a false accusation?
ranking.humanStory: A reviewer traces a claimed result through exact receipt digests and receives one honest state: verified, integrity rejected, or not observable.
ranking.whyNext: Trust, provenance, and observability are central to enterprise AI adoption. The three-way disposition is compact, distinctive, and reusable across every later evidence story.
ranking.directionRisk: A blockchain-style ledger animation would be misleading. Use a concrete consequential claim, receipt chain, and reviewer decision.
ranking.recommendedPackage: 45-second proof story, receipt-chain explorer, trust infographic, evidence-literacy lesson

ranking.storyTitle: The model could answer. It could not decide what counted.
ranking.hook: Twenty checks stand between an AI request and a result you can actually use.
ranking.humanStory: A model consumer submits a bounded request; authority, credentials, endpoints, provider failures, schema, hashes, usage, timing, and attempt lineage determine whether a normalized response exists.
ranking.whyNext: The topic has very broad demand and the twenty-scenario capability can feed a long-running education series on production model execution.
ranking.directionRisk: The root actor is abstract and the mechanic surface is large. Choose one consequential professional task and show only the checks that materially alter its outcome.
ranking.recommendedPackage: Two-minute foundation film, request-to-receipt demo, production checklist, modular training series
